body:
A01 worker deployment and runner implementation-grade plan

Revision 2 (2026-10-22). This pull request connects the existing A01 workers to the merged Terraform interface, supplies their images and chart, and implements the bounded orchestration and evidence export. Acceptance is offline; the scenario workflow and sweeper are delivered as text for Hari to install.

### Selection and authority

Selected: entry C of #109, named **A01 worker deployment and runner**, on child #114. This updates the unapproved Revision 1 in the same comment, as the later decision explicitly directs. Its previous plan check is evidence for Revision 1, not a check or approval of this revision. The REST records confirm predecessor #111 merged at `0c585db5d2ee202c9c5ab47ec49ae01f83aeb820` and #113 at `4a0acc5d886a12cafdfdeafbe1e71f4d0802bf55`; the latter is the source baseline read for this plan.

Authority, in creation order: #14 body and [revision 4](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/issues/14#issuecomment-6229628298), amended `2026-10-17T04:37:58Z`, with its [approval](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/issues/14#issuecomment-6230419686); #109 body adopting that revision; [#109 decision](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/issues/109#issuecomment-6313658165), which adopts the specified recommendation set and ten runner checks from [the planning draft](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/issues/109#issuecomment-6313328886); [ACR amendment](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/issues/109#issuecomment-6313841552); #114 body incorporating those parent requirements; [#114 long-job decision](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/issues/114#issuecomment-6320840549). [#114 blocker-resolution decision](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/issues/114#issuecomment-6332413257) is the latest authority and directs this revision. The older A01 revisions and unadopted recommendations are not additional requirements.

Rules are applied from [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/blob/4a0acc5d886a12cafdfdeafbe1e71f4d0802bf55/AGENTS.md), [factory.md](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/eventhubs-kafka-dotnet/blob/4a0acc5d886a12cafdfdeafbe1e71f4d0802bf55/docs/agents/factory.md), blueprint ADR-008/012/013/014/017/019, and the .NET standards. In particular, factory.md "Item lifecycle" step 3 states: "A plan is implementation-grade when a lower-reasoning model can execute it without judgement." The new project and required references are retained as approval-only P1s under AGENTS.md "Before opening a pull request" rule 8, listed in the PR description; Hari merges.

### Item template

- Item: A01 entry C, worker deployment and runner; synthetic workload.
- Hypotheses/decision rules: #14 revision 4 unchanged. H1 remains `not_decidable_with_pinned_client_evidence`; C0/H4 is recorded only; live C3/H2/H3 is diagnostic only. The separate component evaluator is not implemented here. Complete valid verifier results alone carry counts; missing counts are never zero. A passing probe does not establish later hypothesis prerequisites.
- Configurations: C0 baseline; C3 changes only LoadGenProducer `socket.timeout.ms` from `60000` to `20000`; `request.timeout.ms=60000`, `message.timeout.ms=300000` remain unchanged.
- Fault: the existing fixed live saturation profile; no adaptive load or component toxic execution.
- Measures: unchanged scenario catalogue; retain delivery errors/latencies, throttle windows, request-timeout/disconnect increments, RTT window p99, and permitted verifier counts. KQL corroborates; it never decides the probe.
- Repeats: probe C0 x5, then only after `outcome=pass`, full C0 x5 and C3 x5; no replacements. Each phase has its own apply/run/export/destroy lifecycle. The profile remains seed `1401`, one producer, stages `100/300/900/1800` attempts/s for `60` seconds each.
- Harness changes: images, chart, `Parchwell.Runner`, deployment admission/fidelity, broker inventory and completion receipts, C3 projection, workflow/sweeper text, tests and operational contracts below.
- Enforced checks: the closed ten-item list below; startup/schema/bounds checks implement those items, not new experiment predicates.
- Estimated cost: retain GBP `11.14`, dated 2026-10-17, low confidence: `15*20+3*30=390` minutes; `390/60*1.56+1=11.14`. Limit GBP `15` cumulative. Deployment requires an updated sourced estimate; persistent ACR/state/network are separately recorded outside the item limit under #109. Offline acceptance incurs no Azure scenario run.
- Expected outcome file: `scenarios/A01/expected.yaml` unchanged, excluded from images, chart inputs, deployment and runner resolution.

### File changes and dependency boundary

Existing files read on main that this plan changes: `Parchwell.slnx`, `Directory.Build.props`, worker `.csproj` files and `Program.cs` files, `LoadGenWorker.cs`, `VerifierWorker.cs`, `VerifierHostOptions.cs`, `StartLine/StartLineHandler.cs`, `Common/Kafka/VerifierKafkaSession.cs`, `VerifyRun/VerifyRunHandler.cs`, `VerifyRun/A01/A01EvidenceRecorder.cs`, `tests/Parchwell.ArchitectureTests/{ProjectModel.cs,Parchwell.ArchitectureTests.csproj}`, `docs/engineering/dotnet.md`, `docs/operations/{scenario-contract,loadgen-contract,verifier-contract,terraform}.md`, `src/Parchwell.LoadGen/Run/Ledger/AssemblyInfo.cs`, `src/Parchwell.Verifier/AssemblyInfo.cs`, `infra/persistent/{locals,outputs}.tf`, `tests/terraform/persistent/main.tftest.hcl`, and `docs/engineering/terraform.md`, and `docs/blueprint.md` sections3/4/9. Read lockfiles before regeneration. The ephemeral Terraform root, existing scenario/profile and core numbered verifier checks are not changed. The persistent storage extension below is expressly authorized by the latest decision; only Hari plans and applies it.

Add `src/Parchwell.Runner/Parchwell.Runner.csproj` (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk`, `OutputType=Exe`) and `tests/Parchwell.Runner.Tests/Parchwell.Runner.Tests.csproj` using the existing xUnit test-project shape. Runtime references only `Parchwell.Scenarios`, `Parchwell.Kafka`, and existing centrally pinned `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` and `YamlDotNet`; it does not reference either worker service. Tests reference Runner; add test-only references to LoadGen and Verifier when exercising real writers/codecs, with `InternalsVisibleTo("Parchwell.Runner.Tests")` in their existing assembly-info files. No new package version is needed. Add both projects to `Parchwell.slnx` and their lockfiles. Add Runner to the existing analyzer-property condition, `ProjectRules.SourceNames` and `ServiceNames`, and ArchitectureTests' project references. Keep every existing assertion and forbidden dependency edge; addition to the project inventory strengthens the existing universal tests.

New Runner feature folder `Run/`, with subfolders `Deployment/` (options, generator, chart rendering and process adapter), `Execution/` (phase state machine, pod observation and worker outcomes), `Cost/` (reservation ledger), `Evidence/` (export manifest and KQL), `Rehearsal/` (finite scripted adapters). All are one Run slice; shared DTOs/interfaces belong in `Run/Contracts/`. The composition root wires those collaborators, so no top-level feature slice calls another slice. `Program.cs` is the composition root. Interfaces only at subprocess, cluster, artifact-store, clock and scenario-source boundaries. `TimeProvider` supplies all clocks. Every subprocess uses `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList`, bounded output and cancellation, with no shell interpolation. Secrets/runtime identifiers never enter public logs or public evidence.

New operation documents/data: `docs/operations/a01-runner.md`, `docs/operations/a01-runtime-limits.json`, `docs/operations/workflows/scenario.yml.txt`, `docs/operations/workflows/sweeper.yml.txt`, `docs/operations/service-tags.json`, `infra/persistent/storage.tf`, `scripts/fetch-service-tags.sh`, `scripts/verify-a01-deployment.sh`, and evidence under `docs/operations/evidence/issue-114/`. New chart files are `charts/parchwell/{Chart.yaml,values.yaml,values.schema.json,templates/_helpers.tpl,templates/serviceaccounts.yaml,templates/jobs.yaml,templates/admission.yaml,templates/generated-values.yaml,templates/networkpolicies.yaml}`. Templates must not contain experiment defaults that supersede generated values.

### Images and generated-value mapping

In both worker projects set `EnableSdkContainerSupport=true`, `ContainerRepository` respectively `parchwell/loadgen` and `parchwell/verifier`, `ContainerUser=1654`, `ContainerWorkingDirectory=/app`, and `ContainerBaseImage=mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:10.0.13-noble@sha256:939555726cae4c916d212323ac3c0792996dcac2614f00e82cc40fcf059e1af3`. The digest is the manifest-list digest returned by MCR's runtime endpoint on 2026-10-21; record the resolved linux/amd64 manifest/config digests in image evidence. Publish with `-r linux-x64 --self-contained false`, `ContainerImageTag=<full 40-character source SHA>`, and archive output for offline validation. Add explicit `Content` items for only `../../scenarios/A01/scenario.yaml` and `../../scenarios/profiles/saturation-ramp.yaml`, linked under `scenarios/` with `CopyToOutputDirectory` and `CopyToPublishDirectory=PreserveNewest`. These are regular image-layer files, not ConfigMap-mounted scenario symlinks.

Image native smoke: add a separate `--image-smoke` dispatch before ordinary host startup in each `Program.cs`; it calls `Confluent.Kafka.Library.VersionString`, confirms both packaged files are regular files, and prints JSON `{ "native_loaded": true, "scenario_files": 2, "uid_expected": 1654 }`, then exits 0. No Kafka/Azure client or credential is constructed. Smoke the archive-loaded image as UID 1654, with no network and a read-only root filesystem. UID is verified by container runtime inspection, not by trusting the JSON field. The normal process path is untouched by this flag.

Runner loads the existing files through `ScenarioLoader`, resolves through `ScenarioResolver` with deployment namespace/client inputs, and calls `HelmValuesGenerator.Generate`. The verifier-context generated version-1 document described below is passed unchanged as the first Helm values file. A separate generated runtime envelope adds only `runtime`, never overwrites the five contract keys (`contract_version`, `scenario_id`, `configuration_id`, `profile`, `kafka`). Runtime contains role-specific comparison documents/hashes, phase/run IDs, worker options, Terraform outputs, image digests, source SHA, admission and artifact names, and the committed service-tag data. `values.schema.json` requires contract version `1`, scenario `A01`, configuration `C0|C3`, and nonempty runtime inputs; schema/type failure is runner check 1 or 4, not a result verdict.

Generate two full contract-version-1 comparison documents, `loadgen-values.yaml` and `verifier-values.yaml`, through the existing resolver/generator, without editing their emitted maps. For LoadGen resolution every declared Kafka role has the admitted producer Pod name as ClientId, exactly as LoadGen Program.cs registers today. For Verifier resolution LoadGenProducer has that producer name and VerifierConsumer has the stable `<run-id>-verifier` ClientId, exactly as Verifier Program.cs registers today; do not change either worker's native identity to make equality pass. The first Helm input is the verifier-context document; the runtime envelope carries both exact UTF-8 documents as strings plus separate SHA-256 values. The chart materializes the role-specific document in each worker's `/deployment/generated-values.yaml` using ConfigMap binaryData so Helm indentation/newline handling cannot alter it. Add `Generation/GeneratedValuesCompatibility.cs` in Scenarios with a method that compares the UTF-8 bytes of `HelmValuesGenerator.Generate(resolved, selectedConfiguration)` with this worker's comparison file. Normalized newline policy is exactly the generator's existing one LF; comparison is otherwise byte-for-byte. LoadGen invokes it after its current resolution and before native producer creation; Verifier verify invokes it after resolution and before its Kafka session. Wire the optional external environment key `PARCHWELL_GENERATED_VALUES_FILE`; chart always supplies it; existing nondeployment tests need not. A present path with missing/different bytes fails execution. This proves all profile fields and role Kafka settings, not only three selected timeouts. Both workers still consume the scenario's real files through their current filesystem adapters.

Mapping is exact: `scenario_id -> LoadGen:ScenarioId/Verifier:ScenarioId`; `configuration_id -> ...:ConfigurationId`; packaged profile is loaded from the definition's `profile`; every generated profile leaf and Kafka role map participates in the compatibility equality. Terraform `eventhubs.namespace_name -> NamespaceName`, `blob.account_url -> BlobEndpoint/BlobServiceUri`, `blob.containers.ledger -> BlobContainer/LedgerContainer` (`ledger`), `blob.containers.verifier -> VerifierContainer` (`verifier`); namespace is `parchwell`. Producer client ID is the admitted producer Pod name; verifier client ID is the stable `<run-id>-verifier`, chosen before start-line/admission and shared by start-line and verify. Verifier Pod names remain provenance and do not override VerifierClientId. Resolve/generate both comparison documents again once the actual producer identity is known, before start-line/release. Start-line does not perform scenario equality because its existing mode does not resolve the scenario; verify performs the verifier-context equality before its Kafka session. Test both actual worker DI resolutions for both C0/C3, assert the VerifierConsumer client.id differs between the two documents, both matching files pass, exchanged files fail, and every emitted profile/Kafka leaf is covered. Runtime expected broker names come only from the independent metadata receipt described below. Hash and retain the actual definition/profile/generated files and image provenance in deployment evidence.

### Chart and admission protocol

Chart metadata: `apiVersion: v2`, `name: parchwell`, `version: 0.1.0`, `type: application`. Render only LoadGen and Verifier, including verifier start-line/verify jobs selected by `runtime.mode`. Service accounts use entry B names and client IDs; annotation `azure.workload.identity/client-id`, pod label `azure.workload.identity/use: "true"`. The webhook supplies Azure token environment; Verifier configuration maps `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` into its existing named options at composition time without copying their values to evidence.

Every Job: `completions: 1`, `parallelism: 1`, `backoffLimit: 0`, `restartPolicy: Never`; no TTL deletion before export. Image is `<login_server>/parchwell/<worker>@sha256:<recorded digest>`. Pod security: UID/GID/fsGroup `1654`, `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, capabilities drop `ALL`, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`, read-only root filesystem. Writable `emptyDir` `/work` and `/tmp`; no privileged/host networking or host mounts. Requests `cpu: "1", memory: 2Gi`; limits `cpu: "3", memory: 12Gi`; `/work` size limit `8Gi`. These are execution design limits, not measured capacity. LoadGen node selector `workload=loadgen` plus exact toleration `workload Equal loadgen NoSchedule`; Verifier `workload=workload`, no loadgen/system toleration. Job and process deadlines are the single literal budget list below. `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30`.

Do not start LoadGen before recording its identity. Add `Run/Input/DeploymentAdmission.cs`: when `PARCHWELL_ADMISSION_FILE` is set, wait before `BuildHost` for a JSON admission file using TimeProvider, at most `180` seconds, polling every `1` second, max file `65536` bytes. Initial ConfigMap contains no release. Runner establishes a Kubernetes list/watch from the returned resourceVersion before creating the Job, records every producer Pod UID/name event for the run, and rejects a lost/expired watch rather than inferring uniqueness from a later snapshot. Observe exactly one producer Pod; name/UID becomes the independent expected identity. Perform start-line, then patch that run's admission ConfigMap with `schema_version:1`, `run_id`, `pod_name`, `pod_uid`, `expected_broker_names` (the inventory names), LoadGen comparison-file SHA-256, `release:true`. Worker compares run/name/UID to downward-API `PARCHWELL_POD_NAME`/`PARCHWELL_POD_UID` and expected run; mismatch, malformed release or deadline exits 1 before output/native construction. On release it supplies `LoadGen:ExpectedInstanceId`, `ActualInstanceId`, `PodName`, `ClientId` all equal to that exact admitted name, and ExpectedBrokerNamesCsv from the inventory names in that release. No host startup occurs with the pre-admission empty broker list. Both runtime comparison files are delivered with the admission ConfigMap update and the LoadGen file hash is verified before release. Admission projection symlinks are allowed only for these deployment inputs; scenario filesystem restrictions remain unchanged.

Observe producer Pod history through completed export; any second UID invalidates the repeat even with no production. No restart/replacement is allowed. Preserve event receipt and worker outcomes. An admission timeout is not a replacement-repeat opportunity.

NetworkPolicies select only `app.kubernetes.io/name=parchwell` workload pods in `parchwell`, with both ingress/egress default deny. Allow Event Hubs endpoint `/32` TCP9093, Blob endpoint `/32` TCP443, and TCP443 to each committed AzureActiveDirectory/AzureMonitor prefix. CoreDNS is one peer with BOTH `namespaceSelector.matchLabels.kubernetes.io/metadata.name=kube-system` AND `podSelector.matchLabels.k8s-app=kube-dns`, UDP/TCP53. No `0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0`, arbitrary HTTPS, Kubernetes API egress, or ACR pod egress is added. Kubelet pulls images; network policy is not tenant-level isolation. Before producer admission the runner verifies the selected DNS pod labels and endpoint IPs against runtime outputs.

The service-tag fetch script takes one explicit Microsoft downloadable JSON URL, downloads once with a `60` second/`16MiB` cap and no retries, extracts ONLY global `AzureActiveDirectory` and `AzureMonitor`, and writes source URL, retrieval UTC, file SHA-256, root change number, tag change numbers and ordinal-sorted unique addressPrefixes. Reject absent/empty/duplicate tag objects or invalid CIDR. Commit that data; never fetch on deployment. Tests validate data/schema and render each prefix exactly once. Maximum retained prefixes per tag `4096`; over-limit fails instead of sampling. Source: Microsoft's [service-tag overview and downloadable JSON](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/service-tags-overview); policy semantics: [Kubernetes NetworkPolicy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/).

### Independent inventory, worker completion and C3

Extend verifier start-line with optional `BrokerInventoryOutputName`. In `VerifierKafkaSession`, retain the successful `Metadata.Brokers` returned by the same independent admin metadata call used for start-line. After successful native cleanup, publish an additional create-only inventory JSON in the verifier container: `schema_version:1`, the six-field identity, `brokers:[{id,host,port,name}]`, source `kafka_metadata`, source commit. Sort by id; expected names are the pinned native broker-name rule `sasl_ssl://<host>:<port>/<id>` (bracket IPv6 hosts). The native implementation is [rdkafka_broker.c v2.16.0, rd_kafka_mk_brokername](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/v2.16.0/src/rdkafka_broker.c#L196-L224); no statistics report supplies this inventory. Max brokers `64`; empty, duplicate ID/name, malformed hostname/port, missing output or failed start-line blocks admission. No widening of Event Hubs permissions on failure. Existing start-line JSON/schema is unchanged; optional inventory absent preserves existing callers.

Extend verifier process bookkeeping without changing existing exit codes: add a separate `VerifierCompletionState` registered in DI, marked only after a mode handler returns normally, carrying returned code and selected mode. Exceptions/cancellation do not mark it. Capture immutable identity/options before disposal; track successful `StopAsync` and disposal independently of the returned invalid-result code. After all cleanup/disposal succeeds and before watchdog disposal, emit one bounded JSON line prefixed `PARCHWELL_COMPLETION ` with `schema_version:1`, mode, run identity (gate uses scenario only), source commit, `handler_exit_code` and `cleanup_completed:true`. Flush stdout. Emit none after host/handler/cleanup/disposal/cancellation failure. Receipt writing failure gives exit1. The actual Kubernetes termination code must equal the receipt code; receipt presence alone never authorizes success. Zero plus complete-valid result permits counts; one plus receipt plus published invalid/incomplete result retains diagnostics and absent counts. Exit124, missing receipt, signal, inconsistent result/exit or OOM is execution failure; any result is retained only as unaccepted diagnostic evidence. Add equivalent normal-completion receipt to LoadGen only after successful publication and cleanup; exit0 and receipt are both required before verify.

Extend `A01EvidenceRecorder` with `RecordC3` calling the same existing projection implementation, while keeping `Record`'s C0-only contract and all its current tests intact. `VerifyRunHandler` dispatches C3 to `RecordC3`, other selections to `Record`. `RecordC3` returns no probe observation; records error codes and window values using exactly the current prerequisites (ledger parse for codes, checks17-26 for windows), increments, overflow handling and diagnostic bounds. It does not modify status, failed checks, counts or checks1-27. Non-A01/non-C3 passed to RecordC3 returns both projections absent. No cross-service judgement is introduced. Update only the A01 projection section of `verifier-contract.md` to state the explicit C0/C3 behavior; preserve probe-gate C0-only identity logic.

### Literal execution budgets and option coverage

Store the following production design inputs in `docs/operations/a01-runtime-limits.json` with `schema_version:1`; they are proposed execution ceilings, not measured capacity or new verdict thresholds. Code reads this file, not scattered fallback defaults. Scenario parsing for every caller: MaxDocumentCharacters `1048576`, MaxNestingDepth `32`, MaxScalarCharacters `65536`, MaxParserEvents `100000`. A test enumerates each existing LoadGen public writable property and each verifier mode's required properties and proves that the rendered environment/runtime source supplies it. Unknown/missing properties fail that coverage test. No synthetic test fixture limit becomes a production default.

LoadGen literal budgets (TimeSpan values serialize as invariant `hh:mm:ss[.fff]`): MaxAttempts `186000`; MaxPayloadBytes `900000`; MaxRowBytes `16384`; MaxManifestBytes `67108864`; MaxLedgerBytes/MaxLedgerReadbackBytes `268435456`; LedgerQueueCapacity `8192`; EvidenceQueueCapacity `2048`; MaxReportBytes/MaxSnapshotCharacters `1048576`; MaxEvidenceFileBytes `134217728`; MaxDiagnostics `100`; MaxBrokerSeries `64`; MaxArtifactBytes `268435456`; MaxAggregateArtifactBytes `1073741824`; MaxScheduleLateness `00:00:01`; ProducerDrainTimeout `00:05:00`; LedgerDrainTimeout `00:00:10`; EvidenceCompletionTimeout/StatisticsCompletionTimeout `00:00:20`; UploadTimeout `00:00:30`; CleanupTimeout `00:00:10`; ProcessLifetimeTimeout `00:11:00`; RequireStatisticsEvidence `true`; RequireRequestEvidence `false` (derived from actual measures and asserted equal). Source root `/app`; output root `/work/loadgen`; group ID `a01-unused-enrichment`; broker names CSV from inventory.

Verifier shared values: MaxOutputBytes `16777216`, MaxDiagnosticsPerCheck `100`, MaxDiagnosticBytes `2048`, CleanupTimeout `00:00:10`, IoTimeout `00:00:10`, MaxInputDepth `32`. Kafka modes: TokenTimeout/MetadataTimeout/WatermarkTimeout `00:00:10`; PollSlice `00:00:00.100`; BlobIoTimeout `00:00:30`; MaxPartitions `32`; source root `/app`. Start-line ProcessLifetime `00:02:00`; verify ProcessLifetime `00:12:00`, SafetyStop `00:10:00`; gate ProcessLifetime `00:01:00`. Verify MaxConsumedRecords `372000`, MaxConsumedBytes `17179869184`, MaxArtifactBytes `268435456`, MaxTotalInputBytes `1073741824`, MaxRowBytes `16777216` (also accommodates escaped native statistics), MaxRowsPerArtifact `372000`, MaxInventoryEntries `186000`, MaxNativeReportBytes `1048576`, MaxBrokerEntries `64`. Gate MaxArtifactBytes `16777216`, MaxTotalInputBytes `83886080`, same parser limits. Actual producer identity fills verifier InstanceId/ExpectedInstanceId/ClientId; the stable `<run-id>-verifier` fills VerifierClientId. VerifierCommit is the full source SHA. StartLineOutputName, BrokerInventoryOutputName, ResultOutputName use `<phase>/<run-id>/start-line.json`, `broker-inventory.json`, `result.json`; ArtifactPrefix follows the existing LoadGen index writer exactly, proved by its real writer test. Gate input paths are five downloaded real result paths; ExpectedRepeats is the independent admission list, not extracted from those results.

Job/process deadlines: LoadGen Job deadline `840` seconds (180 admission +660 execution), verify Job `750`, start-line `150`, gate `90`; execution watchdogs remain `660/720/120/60`. The enclosing repeat deadline is `1500` seconds, including admission/start-line; exceeding it is incomplete execution and cleanup, never a sixth attempt. A phase deadline is `9600` seconds, including at most five repeats, apply cap `900`, export cap `300` and destroy reserve `900`. A phase still must be torn down by the four-hour policy. CLI/API call cap `60` seconds; Pod watch event cap `10000`, event/JSON document `16MiB`; Kubernetes poll `1` second; lost watch fails. No retry for create/produce/phase/apply; read-only API reads allow at most `3` attempts with delays `1,2` seconds within the same call deadline. Durable state/manifest caps are specified below. Evidence total per phase `8GiB`; each downloaded producer artifact `256MiB`, per-repeat input total `1GiB`; log per container `16MiB`; KQL per query `10000` rows/`16MiB` and at most `3` reads, 30-second spacing, inside export budget. Limits exceeded mark evidence incomplete, preserve the reason and available bounded data, and proceed to destroy. No silent successful truncation.

The new arithmetic test proves attempts `186000`, workload duration `240`, parser/size bounds positive, verify required-duration sum `680` seconds <720, start-line sum `70` <120, gate sum `20` <60, all time budgets finite, and maximum repeat/phase counts. The ceiling `372000` is an execution limit of twice the scheduled attempts; exhausting it is an execution failure, not proof of any outcome. It never caps published counts by clipping.

### Runner state machine and enforced checks

Commands: `generate --input <runtime.json> --output <directory>`, `phase --input <runtime.json> --output <directory>`, `gate --input <runtime.json> --output <directory>`, `export --input <runtime.json> --output <directory>`, `destroy --input <runtime.json> --output <directory>`, `sweep --input <runtime.json> --output <directory>`, and `rehearse --output <directory>`. `phase`, `export`, `destroy`, `sweep` production adapters are used only by the protected workflow. `rehearse` uses in-process fake external boundaries and never falls back to real tools, credentials or network. Runtime JSON contains `schema_version`, `source_commit`, `phase` (`probe|C0|C3`), Terraform output objects matching entry B, image receipts, limits file path, cost file path, private backend/tfvars paths, durable-store output/readiness path, explicit `initialize_ledger` boolean, and prior phase evidence paths. Production requires the persistent run-storage output; worker Blob options still use only the ephemeral account. `generate` does not read expected.yaml.

A phase journals each transition locally and commits its durable ledger state before advancing: reservation -> apply-started -> outputs-read -> network/input preflight -> per-repeat admission/start-line/loadgen/verify/export -> phase export -> destroy-started -> destroyed. Mark apply-started before invoking Terraform so partially failed apply still enters cleanup. In `finally`, export what exists and attempt ephemeral destroy with its independently reserved budget; export failure must not bypass destroy. Preserve a cleanup failure as a nonzero terminal outcome with the cleanup receipt, never a successful phase. Run through workflow `always()` fallback export/destroy steps as well. Root-level and phase-level guards prevent a later phase until the previous destroy receipt is complete.

1. **Deployment fidelity.** Implement `Deployment/DeploymentGenerator.cs` and compatibility assertions described above. Reject wrong contract version, selected scenario/configuration, mismatched packaged hashes/generated bytes, wrong image source SHA/digest, and runtime envelope attempts to overwrite generated keys before release. Test actual `ScenarioLoader -> ScenarioResolver -> HelmValuesGenerator -> helm template -> worker options` using C0 and C3. Exact timeout expectations are C0 `60000/60000/300000`, C3 `60000/20000/300000`; profile seed1401 and all leaves equal. Replace expected.yaml with unreadable/poison content in a temporary fixture: generation succeeds and no source read requests it.
2. **One independently admitted producer.** `Execution/PodAdmission.cs` owns list/watch receipt and release. Test 0/1/2 distinct UIDs, same-name/new-UID replacement, second Pod that emits no data, mismatched permit, missing permit, expired watch, cancellation and deadline. Only exactly one recorded matching UID allows producer release; any later second UID makes runner run validity invalid and suppresses accepted counts. Keep all raw verifier output as diagnostic data.
3. **Independent brokers.** `Execution/BrokerInventory.cs` parses only the start-line inventory receipt from independent metadata; forwards all names identically to both workers. Test empty/one/65 brokers, duplicate id/name, malformed receipt, failed start-line, absent inventory and statistics containing a different inventory. Statistics never supplies a fallback. Test pinned native formatting with DNS and IPv6 host examples and actual metadata outputs from the existing local Kafka component fixture.
4. **Explicit inputs/bounds.** `Deployment/WorkerOptions.cs` renders every applicable property above. Fail missing auth inputs at worker startup, missing deployment bounds at generation, and invalid finite/positive limits. Tests at each new numerical bound: below/equal/above; durations sum equality is rejected by existing verifier validator. Existing 600000ms SafetyStop is unchanged. Workload-identity values enter only runtime configuration. No new production credential provider; the durable boundary uses only the existing workflow Azure CLI login.
5. **Start-line and LoadGen completion.** `Execution/RepeatExecutor.cs` creates start-line only after the producer identity is fixed and before its permit.
